newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia puts off Mir repair rehearsal.
newsitem.headline: Russia puts off Mir repair rehearsal.

text.p: Russian Mission Control said it had postponed Tuesday's rehearsal of repairs to the crippled Mir space station to give the crew, whose commander has taken ill, more time to rest before the risky and complex operation.

A Mission Control spokesman told Reuters by telephone: "They need more rest to better perform this difficult operation in orbit. Today the doctors...will again discuss (commander Vasily) Tsibliyev's state of health."

He said the Russian-American crew, who normally work during the Moscow day, would sleep until midday (0800 GMT) on Tuesday as they shifted their sleep cycle before doing the repairs on the Moscow night of Thursday to Friday or Friday to Saturday.

They would put off to a later date Tuesday's planned six-hour dress rehearsal in spacesuits. The repair work is intended to restore electrical power lost during Mir's worst accident in its 11 years in space.

Tsibliyev, 43, who was manoeuvring a remote-controlled cargo craft when it slammed into Mir and punctured one of its modules on June 25, is due to perform the bulk of the tricky recabling operation inside the airless Spektr unit.

He announced to Mission Control on Monday that he had been feeling unwell. Doctors said he was overtired and had a cardiovascular problem -- with his heart, lungs or blood supply. Officials said, however, that it should not affect his work.
